en: Five years have passed since the royal house of Pandragon, proud of a thousand years of history, fled into exile in the mountain kingdom of Dagal after its defeat on the plains of Grates. Rescued by the kingdom's chancellor Draupnir, the heirs of the fallen kingdom dream of rising again. At their head stands one woman: Iyolin, Princess of Pandragon, called the Goddess of Vengeance, who leads the resistance herself and has become a figure of terror to the Imperial army. On day 160 of the year 1207, Iyolin's raiders, a band of Holy Knights, slip into Cutis, now Imperial territory, to ambush an Imperial convoy carrying Pandragon's stolen treasure, the Scepter of Glory, through western Cutis.

The Kingdom of Cutis met its end alongside Pandragon after the defeat in the last war. But though a nation may fall, do its heroes not remain? Arcia, a young hero and former captain of the royal guard of Cutis, organised a resistance and harried the Empire ceaselessly with guerrilla tactics in the rugged land. With the full support of the people, Arcia's resistance steadily grew, and an uneasy balance held with the Empire, which saw it as a thorn in its side. That fragile balance broke with an incident near the village of Nohot in northern Cutis: an Imperial noble, newly appointed lord of Nohot, was murdered while touring the region. The Empire named Arcia's men as the culprits and launched a great campaign to crush them. To draw the resistance out of the mountains, the Empire raided homes and attacked villages, and countless civilians lost their lives. Torn between duty to the people and the need to avoid a hopeless fight, Arcia's resistance asks the Dagal alliance for help.

The Eight Wonders of Antaria, handed down since ancient times. The ancient temple called the Temple of the Sun, in the far east of Astania, the religious nation of the east, is one of them. Since the fall of Pandragon and Cutis, Astania has suffered endless Imperial invasions. An ancient religious nation ruled by the Pope, it is held together by the Templars of Astania, the knights of the Church, who are said to be the strongest defenders on the continent.

Lying between Imperial territory and Pandragon, Cyrups City long served as a buffer between the two powers, and it used that position to become the greatest trading city on the continent. Its merchants, above all the Granada Trading Company, spread to every corner of the continent, notorious and ever richer. But where there is light there is shadow; it is only natural that the richest city on the continent draws the most vagrants and thieves. Robin, a girl thief raised in the Thieves' Guild since childhood, gets word that new treasures have arrived at the Granada warehouse...

The Silver Arrow alliance, formed around the Kingdom of Pandragon to stand against the Dark Armor alliance of the Gaysir Empire. After the defeat at Grates, it collapsed in an instant with the fall of Pandragon and Cutis. Six years later, the heirs of the fallen nations are about to bring a new Silver Arrow to life.

Building on its victories in Cutis and Astania, the revived Silver Arrow resolves to invade Imperial territory and retake the old lands of Pandragon. The new alliance army gathers the best troops of every nation: the Holy Knights of Pandragon, the warriors of Dagal, the Templars of Astania and the archers of Cutis, under the command of Princess Iyolin, heir of old Pandragon and now a figure of terror to the Empire. It begins a new challenge against the Empire.

Silver Arrow has triumphed in Pandragon and at Thunderdoom. But to enter the Empire it must pass through Trisys and Garad, the Empire's allies, and Trisys is a military power of the desert. For Silver Arrow, unused to desert terrain, it is a dangerous campaign. Draupnir of Castle Dagal plans to sign a military pact with Bifrost, the military power of the north, to press Trisys from two sides, and he sends GS, a ranger from Bifrost, as his secret envoy...

Beradin's interference ruins Bifrost's intervention, and Iyolin begins the assault on Trisys alone. The desert nation of Trisys is a powerful military state built around Kassim, the King of the Desert, and its elite assassins. By Trisys tradition the throne goes not by birth but to the strongest warrior, and Kassim, who won it that way, is a veteran of countless battles who has survived death many times. Facing a Silver Arrow army flush with victories in Pandragon and Cyrups, the desert army of Trisys leads them to their graves.

If the Granada Trading Company of Cyrups City built its fortune on entrepot trade, the Amigo Trading Company, based in the Pandragon port of Dakama, split the continent's commerce with it through trade across the open sea. But when the Pandragon navy that protected the sea lanes was disbanded after the defeat in the last war, and countless pirates began to operate around the pirate island of Blueseed, the Amigo company's sea trade faced a heavy blow...

Yugdpain, King of Pandragon some three hundred years ago, was a great warrior and a famous adventurer. He studied old books and explored ruins to chronicle the Eight Wonders, and he loved exploring ancient ruins himself. But while exploring the Magic Tower of the Great Lake, one of the Eight Wonders, he vanished, together with the holy sword Stormbringer, one of the Three Treasures of Pandragon. To gather the Three Treasures, said to be the key to breaking the seal of the Twelve Gods, Draupnir sends GS to find the lost holy sword.

Antaria, where war has never ceased for long. As the long wars dragged on, people appeared who made fighting their living. These so-called mercenaries formed an organisation to protect their own interests: the Kashmir. Every mercenary belongs to the Kashmir and signs contracts with clients through it, and any client who mistreats a fellow mercenary must face the swords of every mercenary on the continent. Arcion, the Mercenary King and current captain of the Kashmir, receives an urgent message from Baja of the Amigo Trading Company, his longtime partner and friend, and heads for the port of Dakama...

The holy sword Stormbringer, the Crown of Supremacy and the Scepter of Glory: the Three Treasures of Pandragon, said to hold the secret of breaking the seal of the Twelve Gods. With the recovery of the holy sword lost with Yugdpain, the Three Treasures are united for the first time in three hundred years, and Draupnir and Gishne discover the location of the Citadel of the Sky, where the Twelve Gods are said to be sealed. With Iyolin and the best of Silver Arrow lost in the defeat at Trisys, their last hope lies in the help of the gods. In Dagal, a band of Irregular Knights, mostly mercenaries, is formed around GS, and they set out across the distant sea for the sealed place, following the clues of the Three Treasures.

Across thousands of years, the sealed place is awakened by GS, Rashid and their companions. There remained the bodies of the Twelve Gods, who sealed themselves away after being driven back by the god of destruction in Ragnarok two thousand years ago. Through his communion with the Twelve Gods, GS hears the secret history of Genesis, and the Twelve Gods promise to help GS stop Beradin's plot to revive the god of destruction. And the sealed land, the Citadel of the Sky, begins to move: it was a gigantic airship. Now a great war that will decide the fate of the continent of Antaria is about to begin.

The tremendous power of the Citadel of the Sky overwhelms the Imperial army, and the Irregular Knights destroy the Imperial fortresses one by one. But as GS and his companions stand at the gates of the Imperial homeland, an envoy of the Empire arrives. In exchange for Princess Iyolin, held prisoner, he proposes a private meeting between the Black Prince and GS.
